result.summary:
A mutable top-level variable imported through an api can now be read, assigned and read back on the compiled path. Ledger row 320 turned out to be two defects, and the rung repaired only the one that is the variable's.

Mutability was dropped twice on the way across the api boundary. First in the checker: Operators.scala:444 asked the importing component's own type environment whether an api-qualified name was mutable, so every assignment to an imported mutable variable was refused with "Cannot assign to immutable variable" before codegen was ever reached - a third failure mode the row did not name. STypeChecker already had four api-aware lookups doing exactly the right thing (:307, :324, :334, :356); the fix is a fifth, isMutableName. Then in codegen: forVarRef's fresh-import path always built a plain StaticBinding with the value's descriptor, while a mutable variable's singleton field holds R1's MutableFValue cell, so the run died with NoSuchFieldError. addTopLevelVarBinding:5945-5951 already made that branch for a component's own variables; forVarRef now makes it too.

The class-name half is deliberately untouched, because the measurement contradicts the batch record. An exported function fails identically (NoClassDefFoundError: FnApi), and through the real entry points the divergence never reaches codegen at all: fortress link and walk both refuse a differently-named component outright. The assumption belongs to the repository - Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI:72-76 falls back to the api's own name and only a hand-run LinkShell verb can register otherwise. overview.tex:33-35 settles it, and the repair is a design change past one rung, which is the stop the batch record named. It now has a gated expected-failure test covering a variable and a function together.

One correction to the batch's premise: both microGPT apis export corpus immutably from an api sharing its component's name, and that shape already worked, at ZZ32 and at an object type. Row 320 was never on their critical path; what this rung adds for them is the mutable case.

NamingCzar.java is untouched; two files the record did not name are edited instead, and neither is touched by rungs W or B.

result.summary:
Landed. Eight declarations in CompilerBuiltin.fsi and eight one-line bodies in .fss, two in each of trait ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32 and NN64; no .java, no .scala, no ant compileAll. widen sign-extends from ZZ32 and zero-extends from NN32; unsigned and signed reinterpret the bits; narrow throws IntegerOverflow out of range on both sides. Two extras, both inside the files this rung owns: one new native binding, simpleUnsignedIntArith.toLong, because no imported native zero-extended an NN32 into a long; and the body of NN64.coerce(x: NN32), which sign-extended, so an NN32 of 4294967295 became 18446744073709551615 on the compiled path (measured before the edit).

The test was written first and its failure captured before the edit existed: 69 errors, all "Variable <name> is not defined", and Tests run: 2, Failures: 2. After the edit the same two tests give OK (2 tests) and PASS, reconfirmed after a fresh library-order rebuild. 47 assertions, every NN32/NN64 result rendered through .asZZ.asString to stay clear of open ledger row 326.

The out-of-range decision is argued, not assumed.
